questions.stem: Explain the trade-offs involved in choosing the size of a database page.
markingGuide: Larger pages can reduce the number of I/O operations by reading more data at once.
Smaller pages may lead to less wasted space if records are small.
Larger pages can increase the amount of data read unnecessarily if only a small part is needed.
The choice affects the efficiency of the buffer pool.
questions.explanation: Choosing the size of a database page involves trade-offs. Larger pages can reduce the number of I/O operations by reading more data at once, but they can also lead to more data being read than necessary if only a small part is needed. Smaller pages may result in less wasted space if records are small, but they can increase the number of I/O operations. The page size also affects the efficiency of the buffer pool.

questions.stem: Discuss how the buffer pool size can impact the performance of a database system.
markingGuide: A larger buffer pool can cache more pages, reducing disk I/O.
A smaller buffer pool may lead to more frequent disk reads.
The buffer pool size should be balanced with available system memory.

questions.explanation: The buffer pool size impacts database performance by determining how many pages can be cached in memory. A larger buffer pool can reduce disk I/O by caching more pages, while a smaller buffer pool may lead to more frequent disk reads. The buffer pool size should be balanced with available system memory to avoid affecting other processes. Performance gains from a larger buffer pool depend on the workload and access patterns.
